findings.text: Weak boot predicate reports whether node distributed huge allocation is supported, defaulting to affirmative with arch override permitted.
Boot init services establish the early node mask, ready early page lists, run queued handlers, and start early allocation for gigantic states.
Reporting services expose global and per node totals, free and surplus and reserved accounting, aggregate footprint, and per address space usage.
Fork duplication, VMA split handling, folio install, and the VMA operation table together provide huge mapping lifecycle callbacks.
TLB collection helper adapts generic gathering to huge mappings and a cgroup helper releases reservation charging over an interval.
Allocator parameter validation exists in two builds, one clearing exclusivity when no size was requested and one empty inline.
Parameter queueing rejects absent input and slot or buffer exhaustion, otherwise stores a copy in a shared buffer with its handler.

Count parsing needs a prior valid size marker, routes plain values to default or parsed state, routes node qualified lists to per node slots with accumulation, and rejects repeats without interleaving size.
Size parsing validates arch support, tolerates a repeat only for the unset default state, otherwise creates a new state and arms the marker for a following count.
Default size parsing is accepted once, selects the default index, transfers any early default counts including per node values, then clears the staging count.
Clearing of staged counts targets default storage when no parsed maximum exists and parsed state storage otherwise.
Thread count parsing requires a successful numeric conversion and a nonzero value before updating the stored allocation thread count.
Global reporting is suppressed when huge pages are unsupported; detailed lines cover only the default state while the aggregate sums every state.
Open shares a private reservation by reference counting and ensures a fresh per VMA lock for sharable mappings; close releases only owner reservations after adjusting for already accounted regions.
Split permission requires huge alignment; unsharing walks in large steps, skips absent entries, and unshares each present table under its table lock.
Range copy distinguishes absent, poison, migration, marker, and present entries, skips absent spans and shared tables efficiently, and write protects source on copy on write.
Folio installation marks currency, links anonymous reverse mapping, preserves userfault protection including read write tracking, publishes the entry, accounts the mapping, and marks migratability.
Reservation uncharging is skipped when disabled or when map, counter, or subsystem reference is missing, otherwise it releases proportional charging and drops the reference.
Gathering for huge mappings performs generic collection then records the uniform huge page size of the mapping.
Page size query returns the size of the mapping state; userfault eligibility is always granted; the legacy fault path always traps.
Unsharing either acquires VMA and file mapping write locks internally or asserts the mapping lock is already held, always holding the table lock around each unshare.
Split time unsharing runs with address space, VMA, and mapping locks already held by the caller and therefore requests no additional higher level locks.
Copying holds a write sequence and notifier span for copy on write sources and a read VMA lock for shared sources, plus nested source and destination table locks per address.
Entry moving secures the destination table lock first and then the source lock in nested mode when the two locks differ.
The VMA operation table binds fault, open, close, split approval, page size, and optionally userfault operations for huge mappings.
The userfault operation structure for huge mappings supplies a single eligibility callback.
Observed state fields include maximum, current, free, reserved, surplus, and per node counts plus allocation cursor and queued command value with handler.
Boot flows from node mask setup to early list init, queued handler dispatch with allocator validation, then per state cursor init and gigantic allocation.
Command parsing moves through size validity, parsed state selection, default once flag, and last destination tracking to pair each count with its size.
Anonymous duplication failure drops table locks, allocates and copies outside locks, relocks, revalidates source stability, then either installs or retries.
Reservation ownership starts with a shared reference on open and ends on close with counter release, subpool return, global adjustment, and reference drop.
Boot command handlers for counts, sizes, default size, and allocation threads are invoked through the deferred parameter queue.
VMA callbacks for open, close, split approval, page size, fault, and userfault eligibility enter through the huge VMA operation table.
Malformed count input discards all previously staged per node counts rather than preserving partial values.
Invoking the legacy fault callback unconditionally traps instead of handling the fault.
Splitting inside a large aligned interval without first unsharing the surrounding span can leave stale shared tables, so the boundary case proactively unshares.
Node qualified counts are ignored when the platform lacks support and rejected when the node is out of range or offline.
Duplicating pinned anonymous mappings prone to copy on write must allocate and copy without table locks to avoid sleeping under spinlocks.
Page to kilobyte conversion shifts by page shift minus ten.
Memory reports present sizes in kilobytes using a one kilobyte divisor for totals and per node values.
Setup handlers signal success with zero, benign ignore with one, and malformed input with invalid error.
Sharing and unsharing granularity is one large aligned block stepped and masked with the platform block size and mask.
